title: Member slot assignment service
goal: Assign and persist stable per-session member slots (integer >= 0): the lowest free slot at a member's first join, stable for the session's life, never reused by a different member.
scope_in: `SlotService.assign(sessionId, memberId)` idempotent, race-safe, bounded by the hard cap of 50 members per session.
Migration for `session_member_slots` with unique `(session_id, slot)` and `(session_id, member_id)`.
Purge helper `deleteForSession(sessionId)` for the retention job.
scope_out: Slot to colour mapping - a client presentation rule per CT-WS-SESSION-EVENTS.
Join authorisation and room membership (B043), welcome frame construction (B038).
build_against: Postgres via the B010 harness and the factories for sessions/memberships; no relay running - tests call the service directly and 50 parallel joins are simulated with Promise.all.
interfaces: TS: `interface SlotService { assign(sessionId: string, memberId: string): Promise<number>; get(sessionId: string, memberId: string): Promise<number | null>; list(sessionId: string): Promise<Array<{ memberId: string; slot: number }>>; deleteForSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>; }`

DB: `session_member_slots(session_id text, member_id text, slot int check (slot between 0 and 49), assigned_at timestamptz, primary key(session_id, member_id), unique(session_id, slot))` and `sessions.next_slot int` (or equivalent counter row).
Error: `SlotsExhaustedError` (maps to the registry forbidden-class error) when 50 distinct members already hold slots.
acceptance: The first member in a session gets slot 0, the next 1, then 2; calling `assign` again for an existing member returns the same slot.
50 concurrent `assign` calls for 50 distinct members return exactly the set {0..49} with no duplicates; a 51st distinct member throws `SlotsExhaustedError`.
A member who leaves and a new member who joins afterwards: the new member gets a higher slot; the old slot is not reassigned to anyone else, and the original member rejoining gets the original slot.
`assign` p95 < 10 ms on the Postgres test container.
Deleting the session's slots removes all rows and resets nothing for other sessions.
tests: slots.concurrency.test.ts: 50 and 51 parallel joins (property test with random join orders).
slots.no-reuse.test.ts: leave/join interleavings never reuse a slot.
guardrails: A slot MUST NEVER be reassigned to a different member within a session, even after the original leaves or is kicked (CT-WS-SESSION-EVENTS member slots rule).
Assignment MUST be atomic in the database (counter update or unique-constraint retry), not an in-process counter, so multiple relay nodes cannot collide.
MUST NOT store names, colours or any profile data in the slot table; ids only.
The server MUST NOT send colours; only integer slots leave this service.
failure_modes: Unique violation on concurrent assign -> retry up to 3 times, then surface a retryable 503-class error; never return a slot that is not committed.
DB timeout (2 s) -> error to caller; no slot cached in memory.
notes: Placed under apps/relay because the relay is its only caller (welcome frame and member_joined); the DB access goes through packages/db. CONTRACT GAP: the contract does not say how slots behave when the same user joins from two devices; this card keys slots by member id, so both devices share one slot.
